headline_marked: [[630GB of iPhone 18 Pro supplier data leaked]] from Tata Electronics cyberattack
headline: 630GB of iPhone 18 Pro supplier data leaked from Tata Electronics cyberattack
summary: A cyberattack on Apple supplier Tata Electronics reportedly exposed over 630GB of sensitive data, including details on hundreds of iPhone 18 Pro components and their suppliers. This breach could impact Apple's future negotiations.
details: A cyberattack on Apple's key supplier, Tata Electronics, has reportedly exposed over 630GB of sensitive data. The leaked information, now circulating on the dark web, includes critical details about the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro.

According to Reuters, the breach revealed specifics on hundreds of iPhone 18 Pro parts. This includes chips on the main circuit board, as well as elements of the smartphone's battery and cameras, along with their respective suppliers.

While other Tata clients like Tesla and TSMC also had documents in the leak, a significant portion of the exposed information appears to center on Apple. Tata Electronics has become one of Apple's most prominent manufacturing partners outside of China.

Apple has stated it is investigating the incident and is working with Tata on long-term security measures. The exposure of these supplier relationships could potentially put Apple at a disadvantage in future negotiations, especially amid rising product prices due to RAM shortages.

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to be announced this fall, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro Max and potentially Apple's first foldable smartphone. This leak provides an early, unauthorized glimpse into its manufacturing ecosystem.
